hero.title: µWebZockets
hero.summary: A zero-allocation, shared-nothing server framework for Zig. HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, WebSocket, and RPC through one type-safe `Request`/`Response` API.

dictionary.label: Dictionary entry for the word fast

lines.definitionTwo: 2. Zig で HTTP、WebSocket、RPC をゼロアロケーションで処理する。

server.label: 04 / Server
server.heading: Use µWZ as your server
server.intro: Keep the Zig application you already have. The runtime takes over transport, TLS, limits, and shutdown without changing how your handlers are written.

addPackage.title: Add the package
addPackage.text: Fetch the pinned dependencies through the Zig package manager. No CMake, Ninja, Go, Perl, Python, or system zlib.

mountHandlers.title: Mount your handlers
mountHandlers.text: Register HTTP, WebSocket, RPC, and static routes on one app. Your handlers stay ordinary Zig functions.

runWhereYouDeploy.title: Run where you deploy
runWhereYouDeploy.text: Start one process or a thread-per-core cluster. Each worker owns its event loop, slab set, and physical core affinity where the platform allows.

server.ctaText: Bring your routes. The runtime owns transport, TLS, limits, and shutdown.

author.label: 05 / Author
author.name: Noah Trần
author.bio: Noah Trần is a software engineer based in Ho Chi Minh, working across Svelte, Astro, Zig, Rust, design, and framework/tooling. They are the creator of [Hope Art](https://hope-art.app) and now author and lead maintainer of [Farben](https://github.com/farbenbuilds).

indexCards.heading: Start here.
indexCards.intro: Six ways into the runtime: install it, learn the ownership rule, migrate a service, configure the server, understand the worker model, or explore type-safety.

gettingStarted.description: Install the package and run your first server.

shareNothing.title: Share nothing rule
shareNothing.description: One worker, one event loop, one slab set, no shared state.

migrate.title: Migrate existing projects
migrate.description: Bring an existing Zig service onto the runtime.

configure.title: Configure a uWZ server
configure.description: Set capacities, TLS, routes, and lifecycle explicitly.

clusterWorker.title: Understand a Cluster/Worker
clusterWorker.description: Follow how workers share ports and own their state.

typeSafety.title: Explore Type-safety
typeSafety.description: See how typed requests, responses, and routes stay checked at compile time.

support.label: 02 / Support
support.heading: What µWZ supports
support.intro: One server surface for the transports a Zig service actually needs, with the same routing, limits, and lifecycle across each one.

http.title: HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2
http.text: Persistent connections, streaming bodies, multiplexed streams, and TLS ALPN in one handler model.

http3.title: HTTP/3
http3.text: QUIC over UDP with the same routing and handlers as the TCP transports. QUIC clustering is not supported.

webSocket.title: WebSocket
webSocket.text: RFC 6455 with compression, pub/sub, and heartbeats for long-lived connections.

rpc.title: RPC
rpc.text: Typed request and response calls that share the app, limits, and worker model.

tls.title: TLS
tls.text: Ephemeral and production credentials, ALPN, 0-RTT, and mutual TLS.

staticAssets.title: Static assets
staticAssets.text: Serve files from the same process instead of adding a second asset server.

workers.title: Thread-per-core workers
workers.text: Shared-nothing workers with one event loop each, pinned to physical cores where the platform allows.

zeroAllocation.title: Zero allocation
zeroAllocation.text: Bounded startup slabs and explicit capacity limits on every request path.

support.platformNote: Linux runs the hosted runtime matrix; macOS is supported and cross-compiled; Windows is compile-checked.
